# EntropySource

Something that can fill a buffer with unpredictable bytes.

```rux
pub interface EntropySource {
    func Fill(
        self: &var Self,
        buffer: *var opaque,
        length: uint
    ) -> ! EntropyError;
}
```

Implemented by [`SystemEntropy`](/docs/api/entropy/system-entropy) for the operating system's generator, and by a test for a source that fails on
demand. An implementation either fills the whole buffer and succeeds, or fails with why it did not.

## Requirements

<h3 id="fill"><code>Fill</code></h3>

```rux
func Fill(
    self: &var Self,
    buffer: *var opaque,
    length: uint
) -> ! EntropyError
```

Fills `length` bytes of `buffer` with unpredictable bytes.
`buffer` is borrowed and written; `length` is read by value. Succeeds only when every byte was written. An
implementation may write part of the buffer before failing — the caller is what guarantees nothing
partial survives.
`buffer` must be writable for `length` bytes.

| Name     | Type          | Description            |
| -------- | ------------- | ---------------------- |
| `buffer` | `*var opaque` | receives the bytes     |
| `length` | `uint`        | how many bytes to fill |

**Returns**: nothing when every byte was written, or why not

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Entropy/Src/Fill.rux#L28)

## Related

<h3 id="fill-from"><code>FillFrom</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FillFrom(
    source: &var EntropySource,
    buffer: *var opaque,
    length: uint
) -> ! EntropyError
```

Fills `length` bytes of `buffer` from `source`, in as many calls as it takes.
`source` is borrowed for the call; `buffer` is borrowed and written; `length` is read by value. Succeeds only when
every byte was written, and otherwise fails with what the source reported.
A request larger than a single call accepts is split, so a caller need not know what that limit is. A failure
part-way through a split request is a failure of the whole request: there is no state in which some of a buffer
is unpredictable and the rest is not, because nothing downstream could act on the difference.
Runs in time proportional to `length` and allocates nothing.
`buffer` must be writable for `length` bytes. On any failure the whole buffer is zeroized, including the parts an
earlier call filled successfully.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Entropy/Src/Fill.rux#L79)

**Parameters**

| Name     | Type                 | Description               |
| -------- | -------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `source` | `&var EntropySource` | where the bytes come from |
| `buffer` | `*var opaque`        | receives the bytes        |
| `length` | `uint`               | how many bytes to fill    |

**Returns**: nothing when every byte was written, or why not

<h3 id="fill-with-retries"><code>FillWithRetries</code></h3>

```rux
pub func FillWithRetries(
    source: &var EntropySource,
    buffer: *var opaque,
    length: uint,
    attempts: uint
) -> ! EntropyError
```

Fills `length` bytes of `buffer` from `source`, trying again while the failure says trying again might work.
`source` is borrowed for the call; `buffer` is borrowed and written; `length` and `attempts` are read by value.
`attempts` is how many extra tries to make, so zero is one attempt and behaves exactly like [`FillFrom`](/docs/api/entropy/entropy-source#fill-from).
Only a transient failure is retried — `Interrupted`, which says a signal arrived rather than that anything is
wrong. A system with no source and a provider that refused are both reported at once, because repeating them
would only take longer to reach the same answer.
Runs in time proportional to `length` times the attempts made, and allocates nothing.
`buffer` must be writable for `length` bytes. Every failed attempt zeroizes the buffer, so a failure that
exhausts the attempts leaves zeros.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Entropy/Src/Fill.rux#L113)

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type                 | Description                                                         |
| ---------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source`   | `&var EntropySource` | where the bytes come from                                           |
| `buffer`   | `*var opaque`        | receives the bytes                                                  |
| `length`   | `uint`               | how many bytes to fill                                              |
| `attempts` | `uint`               | how many times to go back to an interrupted source before giving up |

**Returns**: nothing when every byte was written, or why not — `Interrupted` after `attempts` tries
